Consult Summary:
- Video consult for new right knee pain and clicking during exercise with occasional transient toe tingling after runs.
- Advice given: rest modification, ice therapy, avoid running through pain, physiotherapy referral, possible imaging pending assessment, stronger anti-inflammatory prescribed, red flag precautions reviewed.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Right knee pain with clicking during exercise (onset ~2 weeks ago). Triggered after ~20 minutes of running; last run required stopping due to worsening pain.
- Associated features: initial mild swelling after first run resolved with ice; clicking noted during gym abdominal exercises requiring knee flexion/extension; currently no pain at rest.
- Pertinent negatives: no true giving way, no locking, no problems on stairs or walking, full flexion/extension possible, no persistent swelling, no redness/heat reported.
- Context: increased training for a marathon (runs 4–8 miles; began ~1 month ago); prior ice hockey fall with large bruise a few months ago.
- Examination: none performed via video.
- Clinical impression/differential discussed: undifferentiated right knee pain associated with running; clinician advised possible need for imaging to assess cartilage; ACL or other internal derangement cannot be diagnosed over video.
- Plan: continue ice therapy; reduce/ease up on running and do not run through pain; prescribe a stronger anti-inflammatory to take regularly (not with ibuprofen; take with food); referral to physiotherapy for assessment and management; consider imaging after assessment; attend clinic if physio wait is long. Red flags for urgent review: persistent swelling, heat/redness, fever/feeling unwell, or complete locking/inability to bend/straighten.

Issue 2:
- Transient tingling in right toes after a run (single episode, resolved).
- Pertinent negatives: no ongoing altered sensation, no color or temperature change in lower legs, no calf pain, no foot/arch joint pain, no difficulty on hard floors.
- Plan: No specific treatment discussed during this visit.

Issue 3:
- Intermittent lower leg indentation from socks after prolonged standing (self-reported). Pitting not tested.
- No associated calf pain reported.
- Plan: No specific management discussed.

Medications:
- Ibuprofen up to 400 mg as needed for joint pain.
- Aleve (medication per patient; exact agent/dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Vitamin D (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Melatonin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Xanax (alprazolam) occasionally for sleep (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- New prescription: stronger anti-inflammatory sent to pharmacy; name/dose/route/frequency not documented. Advised not to take with ibuprofen and to take with food.

Allergies:
- Not documented.

Past Medical History:
- Farsighted; prior LASIK surgery.
- History of severe urinary tract infection; evaluated in ER for possible kidney stones (no outcome documented).
- Prior sports injury (ice hockey fall with large bruise) a few months ago.

Social History:
- Training for a marathon; runs 4–8 miles; regular gym workouts.
- Plays ice hockey.
- Occasionally smokes cannabis (“smoke a joint”).
- Tobacco and alcohol use not documented.
- Living arrangements not documented.

Preventative History:
- Not discussed: cervical screening, mammogram, prostate blood test, fecal occult blood test, bone density, vaccinations, optometry review (besides prior LASIK), skin check, or other preventive care.

Physical Examination:
- No vitals documented.
- No in-person physical examination performed during video visit.

Plan:
- Continue frequent ice therapy to the knee.
- Modify training: ease up on running; do not run through pain.
- Start prescribed stronger anti-inflammatory instead of ibuprofen; take with food; do not combine with ibuprofen.
- Physiotherapy referral for comprehensive knee assessment and management.
- Consider imaging (e.g., to evaluate cartilage) after assessment if indicated.
- If physiotherapy wait is long, attend clinic for in-person examination.
- Urgent care advice: seek immediate review if knee develops persistent swelling, heat, redness, fever/feeling unwell, or if the knee locks and cannot bend/straighten.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: allergies not documented; no vitals; no physical exam; medication doses/frequencies largely unspecified; tobacco and alcohol use not documented; detailed past surgical history beyond LASIK not documented.
- Internal conflicts: clinician referenced “both knees,” but patient clarified pain is primarily in the right knee (conflict noted). Patient uncertain about the active ingredient in Aleve.
- Transcript quality: generally clear; minor interruptions and filler speech; no major inaudible sections.
